stories.hook: ¿La anhedonia empeora el pronóstico de la depresión?
stories.headline: Los pacientes con depresión y anhedonia presentan mayor carga clínica y menor remisión
stories.finding: Los pacientes con anhedonia (n=4,255) mostraron tasas de remisión más bajas en el año posterior al índice que los pacientes sin anhedonia (n=1,454). Además, presentaron patrones de tratamiento más intensivos y mayor persistencia de síntomas.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya la necesidad de identificar la anhedonia en la práctica clínica y de diseñar intervenciones específicas, pues su presencia se asocia a peor pronóstico y mayor consumo de recursos sanitarios.
stories.paperTitle: Clinical burden of major depressive disorder with versus without prominent anhedonia using a real-world electronic health records and claims linked database
stories.originalAbstract: BACKGROUND: Anhedonia is a core feature of major depressive disorder (MDD), yet the clinical burden in real-world settings is not well understood. This retrospective cohort study assessed depression symptoms and treatment patterns among patients with MDD with and without prominent anhedonia. METHODS: Patients with MDD were selected from a real-world dataset of electronic health records from mental health specialists and linked medical and pharmacy claims (OM1, Inc. Boston MA) between January 2013 through August 2023. Patients were included if the first Patient Health Questionnaire 9-item (PHQ-9) score indicated moderate to severe depression (≥ 10) with a MDD diagnosis +/-30 days. The date of the patients’ first PHQ-9 score was used as the index date. Patients with a score ≥ 2 on PHQ-9 item 1 (anhedonia) at the index date were classified as MDD with prominent anhedonia (MDD-ANH) (n = 4,255). The remaining patients were classified as Other-MDD (n = 1,454). Treatment patterns were assessed using prescription records in the year following the index date. The last PHQ-9 score in the year following the index date was used to assess remission rates (PHQ-9 score < 5) or persistence of moderate to severe depression. RESULTS: A total of 5,709 patients with MDD were assessed; 74.5% were in MDD-ANH and 25.5% were in the Other-MDD cohort (met criteria for MDD but not prominent anhedonia). The mean index PHQ-9 score was 18.2 (SD = 4.2) for MDD-ANH patients and 13.5 (SD = 2.9) for Other-MDD patients. The percentage of patients treated with antidepressants was 86.4% in the MDD-ANH group and 84.7% in the Other-MDD group. After adjusting for baseline characteristics, patients with MDD-ANH were more likely to have been treated with atypical antipsychotics (OR = 1.51, p < 0.001), more likely to have switched medication (OR = 1.24, p = 0.004), and more likely to have augmented antidepressant therapy (OR = 1.16, p = 0.021) than Other-MDD patients. Patients with MDD-ANH were less likely to have achieved remission (OR = 0.82, p = 0.003) and were more likely to have persistent depression (OR = 1.50, p < 0.001) than patients with Other-MDD. CONCLUSIONS: Overall, MDD-ANH patients had higher clinical burden reflected in more depressive symptoms, higher treatment utilization and lower rates of remission compared to Other-MDD.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué el pensamiento excesivo perjudica el aprendizaje?
stories.headline: Creencias metacognitivas sobre la preocupación dañan la función ejecutiva
stories.finding: En 275 adolescentes, las creencias metacognitivas disfuncionales y las estrategias de regulación emocional maladaptativas se asociaron significativamente con peor funcionamiento ejecutivo. A su vez, el deterioro ejecutivo se relacionó negativamente con el rendimiento académico.
stories.takeaway: Identificar y modificar estas creencias y estrategias puede mejorar la función ejecutiva y, con ello, el desempeño escolar, ofreciendo un objetivo terapéutico concreto contra la rumiación en jóvenes.
stories.paperTitle: Trait Anxiety, Emotion Regulation, and Metacognitive Beliefs: An Observational Study Incorporating Separate Network and Correlation Analyses to Examine Associations with Executive Functions and Academic Achievement
stories.originalAbstract: Trait anxiety, emotion regulation strategies, and metacognitive beliefs influence executive functions (EFs) and academic achievement. This study examines their interplay and impact on academic success. In total, 275 adolescents (10–17 years) and parents completed an online questionnaire assessing trait anxiety, emotion regulation strategies, metacognition, parent-reported behaviors related to executive functioning, and overall school average. Preliminary analyses confirmed consistency with the existing literature for each variable and their interaction. Furthermore, we conducted a network analysis among the main variables. This analysis supports the need to pay more attention to reflective variables—maladaptive emotion regulation strategies and metacognitive beliefs about worry—when studying trait anxiety. These variables were linked to problematic executive functioning in adolescents, and the latter was negatively linked to academic achievement. This study offers innovative insights by investigating relationships less explored in the scientific literature. It reveals high and significant correlations between metacognitive beliefs, maladaptive emotion regulation strategies, and trait anxiety (r > 0.500, p < 0.001) but also between these variables and both executive functioning and academic achievement. These findings offer new perspectives for research and underscore the importance of holistically examining the psychological factors related to academic success.

stories.hook: ¿Por qué la prosopagnosia aumenta la ansiedad social?
stories.headline: Alto 44 % de ansiedad social clínica en personas con prosopagnosia
stories.finding: Los participantes con prosopagnosia desarrollativa mostraron síntomas de ansiedad social significativamente mayores (M = 30,25) que los controles (M = 17,19), y el 44 % superó el umbral clínico frente al 14 % de los controles. Además, la extraversión y menores rasgos autistas se asociaron a niveles más bajos de ansiedad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo alerta a clínicos sobre la alta vulnerabilidad a la ansiedad social en la prosopagnosia, sugiriendo la necesidad de evaluar y tratar este componente para mejorar la calidad de vida y la interacción social de estos pacientes.
stories.paperTitle: Social Interaction Anxiety in Developmental Prosopagnosia: Prevalence, Severity, and Individual Differences
stories.originalAbstract: OBJECTIVE: Although elevated social anxiety in developmental prosopagnosia (DP) has been reported in anecdotal and qualitative studies, the current study sought to better quantify the prevalence, severity, and moderators of social anxiety in a large DP sample. METHOD: A total of 88 DPs and 58 controls completed the validated Social Interaction Anxiety Scale and assessments of face recognition, autism traits, personality (Big Five Inventory), and coping strategies. RESULTS: DPs reported greater social anxiety symptoms (M = 30.25) than controls (M = 17.19), with 44% of DPs above a probable clinical cutoff compared with 14% of controls. Exploratory analyses revealed that DPs' social anxiety was more specific to items pertaining to mixing socially or interacting with unfamiliar people. Notably, several DPs reported minimal social anxiety, which was associated with being more extraverted and having fewer autism traits. A follow-up survey revealed that extraverted DPs more openly disclosed face recognition inabilities than introverted DPs, which may be a factor in their reduced social anxiety. CONCLUSION: These results better quantify the potential serious psychosocial consequences of DP and highlight the importance of individual differences as well as targeted intervention.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la realidad virtual superar al tratamiento tradicional en la ansiedad social?
stories.headline: La realidad virtual reduce la ansiedad social más que la lista de espera
stories.finding: Un meta‑análisis de 17 ensayos controlados aleatorizados mostró que la terapia de exposición en realidad virtual supera a la lista de espera al reducir la ansiedad social al final del tratamiento y en el seguimiento. Es comparable a otras intervenciones y se intensifica en casos sintomáticos al añadirse componentes cognitivos.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo respalda el uso de la realidad virtual como alternativa eficaz y escalable para tratar la ansiedad social, ofreciendo una opción que puede implementarse cuando los recursos tradicionales son limitados y potencialmente mejorar la adherencia y resultados clínicos.
stories.paperTitle: Virtual reality exposure therapy for social anxiety disorders: a meta-analysis and meta-regression of randomized controlled trials
stories.originalAbstract: Background and objectives Virtual reality exposure therapy offers a unique opportunity to treat social anxiety disorder. This meta-analysis aims to evaluate the effectiveness of virtual reality exposure therapy compared to waitlist comparators or other interventions for individuals with social anxiety disorder in alleviating anxiety symptoms.Methods A three-step comprehensive search for the randomized controlled trials of virtual reality exposure therapy was conducted from inception to 7 December 2023. The overall effect was measured using Hedges’ g and determined using t-statistics at a significance level of p < 0.05. Sensitivity, subgroup, and meta-regression analyses were carried out.Results A total of 17 randomized control trials were retrieved from nine electronic databases. Virtual reality exposure therapy has greater efficacy than waitlist comparators in reducing anxiety symptoms at post-intervention and follow-up assessment. Virtual reality exposure therapy demonstrates a similar effect to other interventions at post-intervention and follow-up assessment. We observed a greater effect for participants with symptomatic social anxiety when we combined the intervention with cognitive behavioral therapy compared to its counterpart. Meta-regression analyses found no significant covariate.Conclusions Overall, virtual reality exposure therapy can provide supplementary therapy for improving anxiety symptoms. Additional high-quality and large-scale trials with long-term follow-up are needed.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la confianza epistémica proteger a adolescentes con trauma?
stories.headline: La confianza epistémica y la mentalización amortiguan el impacto de ACEs en adolescentes
stories.finding: En adolescentes no clínicos, los niveles de ACEs se asociaron positivamente con la maladaptación psicológica. Sin embargo, la confianza epistémica, la afectividad mentalizada y el funcionamiento reflexivo intervinieron como mediadores protectores, atenuando esa asociación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fortalecer la confianza epistémica y la capacidad de mentalizar emociones puede ser una estrategia terapéutica eficaz para mitigar los efectos de experiencias adversas tempranas en la salud mental de los adolescentes.
stories.paperTitle: Adverse childhood experiences and psychological maladjustment in adolescence: The protective role of epistemic trust, mentalized affectivity, and reflective functioning
stories.originalAbstract: INTRODUCTION: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are psychosocial factors acknowledged as significant contributors to health consequences later in adolescence, including psychological maladjustment. The research suggests that, at a transdiagnostic and transtheoretical level, working on restoring epistemic trust (ET), mentalized affectivity (MA), and reflective functioning (RF) in adolescents with ACEs assumes a central role in the therapeutic process. However, there are still few studies that attempted to investigate the specific role of these sociocognitive factors in the detrimental positive association between levels of experienced ACEs during childhood and psychological maladjustment in nonclinical adolescents. METHODS: = 16.1, SD = 1.64) self-reported ACEs (Childhood Trauma Questionnaire-Short Form), psychological maladjustment (Strengths and Difficulties Questionnaire), ET (Epistemic Trust, Mistrust and Credulity Questionnaire), MA (Brief-Mentalized Affectivity Scale for Adolescence), and RF (Reflective Functioning Questionnaire). A multiple mediation regression analysis has been performed to explore the association between ACEs and psychological maladjustment through the interaction with socio-cognitive factors. RESULTS: ACEs are positive predictors of psychological maladjustment later in adolescence. Regardless of gender differences, epistemic mistrust and credulity, processing and expressing emotions, and uncertainty about mental states mediated this association, while epistemic trust, identifying emotions, and certainty about mental states did not configure as significant mediators. CONCLUSION: Findings suggest that ET disruptions and deficits in RF are risk factors, while MA is a protective factor within the link between ACEs and psychological maladjustment in adolescence. These links help to specify the role of sociocognitive factors in the development of mental problems in adolescents who have been exposed to adverse experiences in childhood.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo reparar rupturas de alianza en terapia psicodinámica?
stories.headline: Estrategias específicas reparan rupturas de alianza en terapia breve
stories.finding: El estudio evaluó el modelo de reparación de rupturas de alianza en dos mujeres autolesivas que recibieron terapia psicodinámica breve, analizando sesiones mediante el Working Alliance Inventory y el Rupture Resolution Rating System. Los resultados mostraron que la reparación exitosa dependió de estrategias del camino 1 (aceptación y validación) y del camino 3 (exploración de la ruptura y su vínculo con patrones interpersonales), mientras que las estrategias del camino 2 empeoraron la ruptura en el caso no exitoso.
stories.takeaway: Identificar y aplicar las estrategias de aceptación, validación y exploración de la ruptura permite reparar eficazmente la alianza terapéutica, favoreciendo mejores resultados en pacientes autolesivos y ofreciendo una guía práctica para terapeutas psicodinámicos.
stories.paperTitle: Testing the alliance rupture resolution model in two self-injuring women receiving short-term psychodynamic therapy in a training clinic:Applying task analyses to compare therapeutic strategies in a successful and unsuccessful case
stories.originalAbstract: The study aimed to test and refine the alliance rupture repair model with three pathways outlining how therapists successfully resolve alliance ruptures. The patient-reported Working Alliance Inventory and the was used to select cases and sessions , and the Rupture Resolution Rating System was used to analyze the rupture session and the two following session in each dyad. The results showed that successful repair was linked to pathway 1 strategies, including accept and validation. Moreover, this pathway was a prerequisite for pathways 2 and 3 to work. In fact, pathway 2 strategies of talking about goal and methods seemed to make the rupture even worse in the unsuccessful case. In contrast, pathway 3 strategy of exploring the rupture and linking it to an interpersonal pattern outside therapy was unique for the successful case and highly effective. Clinical implications and common versus specific features of the rupture resolution process in short-term psychodynamic psychotherapy will be discussed.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la atención plena reducir los problemas emocionales de los bomberos?
stories.headline: Facetas de mindfulness vinculadas a menor disfunción emocional en bomberos
stories.finding: En 685 bomberos, no‑juzgar se relacionó negativamente con desafíos de regulación emocional y positivamente con déficits en la conducta dirigida a metas. Actuar con conciencia se asoció a menores déficits de conducta dirigida e impulsividad, mientras que el consumo de alcohol se vinculó a mayor impulsividad.
stories.takeaway: Estos hallazgos sugieren que entrenar facetas específicas de mindfulness, como no‑juzgar y actuar con conciencia, podría mejorar la regulación emocional y reducir impulsividad y consumo de alcohol en bomberos, ofreciendo una vía preventiva en profesiones de alto riesgo.
stories.paperTitle: Network of Mindfulness and Difficulties in Regulating Emotions in Firefighters
stories.originalAbstract: Abstract Objectives Growing evidence supports the role of mindfulness in regulating emotions in the general population. However, the interactive network of mindfulness facets and difficulties in regulating emotions is not well understood, which is specifically important for individuals involved in high-risk professions, such as first responders. The aim of this study was to investigate the interactive relations between mindfulness facets (acting with awareness, non-judging, describing, observing, and non-reacting), ability to regulate emotions and alcohol use in a sample of firefighters, including military veterans. Method A sample of 685 career firefighters, of whom 154 (22.5%) are military veterans, completed measures of mindfulness and difficulties in regulating emotions. The dataset was subjected to network analysis. Results The mindfulness facet non-judging was negatively related to emotion-regulation challenges, such as nonaccepting attitudes and lack of clarity, and positively related to deficits in goal-directed behaviour. Acting with awareness was negatively related to goal-directed behaviour deficits and impulsivity. Alcohol use was positively linked to impulsivity and negatively linked to describing. Overall, emotion-regulation difficulties were positively linked together, and positive links were found between most mindfulness facets. Directed network analysis found non-judging and emotion-regulation strategy as primary predictors. Non-judging acted as a protective factor, supporting other mindfulness facets, while emotion-regulation strategy exacerbated emotion-regulation challenges acted as a risk factor. Conclusions This network analysis demonstrated that acting with awareness and a non-judgmental attitude, facets of mindfulness, are linked to better emotion-regulation and may play protective role against impulsivity and alcohol use.

stories.hook: ¿La calidad del sueño atenua el riesgo de demencia?
stories.headline: La calidad del sueño medía parcialmente la relación entre fragilidad y deterioro cognitivo.
stories.finding: En 2830 adultos mayores, la prevalencia de deterioro cognitivo fue del 21.77 %. El análisis de mediación mostró que la calidad del sueño explica parcialmente la relación entre fragilidad física y deterioro cognitivo, representando el 12.37 % del efecto total.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que mejorar la calidad del sueño puede interrumpir la cadena de fragilidad a deterioro cognitivo, ofreciendo una vía de intervención preventiva en la población mayor.
stories.paperTitle: The Mediating Effect of Sleep Quality on the Relationship Between Frailty and Cognitive Impairment Among Community‐Dwelling Older Adults: A Cross‐Sectional Study
stories.originalAbstract: AIMS: To investigate the relationship between physical frailty and cognitive impairment among community-dwelling older adults and the mediating role of sleep quality in that relationship. DESIGN: Cross-sectional study. METHODS: A convenience sample of 2830 participants aged 60 years and above from Xi'an, China was assessed using the FRAIL scale, Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) and Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Comprehensive data on sociodemographic and health-related covariates were collected. Statistical analyses included chi-square tests, multivariate binary logistic regression, Spearman's correlation and mediation analysis using PROCESS (Model 4) with 5000 bootstraps. RESULTS: The prevalence of cognitive impairment was 21.77%. Cognitive function was negatively correlated with physical frailty and sleep quality, whereas physical frailty was positively correlated with sleep quality. Age ≥ 85 years, middle school education, sleep duration > 8 h and stroke were independently associated with higher odds of cognitive impairment. Sleep quality partially mediated the frailty-cognition relationship, accounting for 12.37% of the total effect. CONCLUSION: Sleep quality partially mediates the relationship between physical frailty and cognitive impairment, highlighting a critical opportunity for nurses to implement targeted sleep hygiene interventions alongside physical frailty management to potentially mitigate cognitive decline in the growing community-dwelling geriatric population. PATIENT OR PUBLIC CONTRIBUTION: No patient or public contribution. IMPLICATIONS FOR NURSING PRACTICE: Nurses should incorporate routine sleep quality screening into standard geriatric health assessments, particularly for frail older adults. In community settings, nurses can take the lead in delivering targeted sleep hygiene education, coordinating multidisciplinary management for underlying sleep disorders, and tailoring interventions to match each patient's frailty severity. IMPACT: These findings highlight the importance of integrating sleep quality assessment into routine geriatric care. For the growing aging population, nurses working in community settings can play a critical role in delivering targeted sleep hygiene interventions and managing physical frailty to potentially help preserve older adults' cognitive function.

stories.headline: Intervención de cognición incorporada eleva la autoeficacia en mujeres
stories.finding: En un ensayo controlado aleatorizado piloto, nueve mujeres recibieron una intervención basada en cognición incorporada y mostraron un mayor aumento de autoeficacia comparado con ocho mujeres en el grupo cognitivo y ocho en control; la diferencia alcanzó d = 0.43 frente al grupo cognitivo y d = 1.04 frente al control.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que trabajar con la experiencia corporal puede ser una estrategia eficaz para fortalecer la autoeficacia y la resiliencia, ofreciendo una alternativa complementaria a las intervenciones puramente cognitivas en la práctica clínica.
stories.paperTitle: The Influence of Embodied Cognition on Self-Efficacy, Self-Accountability, and Resilience in Women Affected by Social Expectations
stories.originalAbstract: Research has explored cognitive-based interventions to enhance psychological constructs; however, emerging evidence regarding embodied cognition principles, which examine how bodily experiences shape our thoughts and behaviors, may provide a more integrative approach. Self-efficacy, self-accountability, and resilience are essential psychological constructs that empower women to navigate challenges, pursue goals, and maintain agency in their lives. The research explored whether embodied cognition interventions (N=9) can disrupt automatic, conformity-driven behaviors and promote increased self-efficacy, self-accountability, and resilience in women compared to techniques that rely solely on cognitive reflection (N=8), or a control group (N=8). Findings from this randomized controlled pilot study did not support statistical significance for most hypotheses, although the effects did go in the anticipated direction, favoring the Embodied Cognition group. Those randomized to the Embodied Cognition group had a larger pre-to-post increase in self-efficacy compared to the Cognitive Only group (Cohen’s d = 0.43) and the Control group (Cohen’s d = 1.04). Similarly, the Embodied Cognition group displayed a larger improvement in resilience than the Cognitive Only (Cohen’s d = 0.50) and Control groups (Cohen’s d = 1.16). Within the Agency sub-category of self-accountability, a statistically significant group x time effect was found as the discrepancy levels decreased as expected. A larger decrease was found in self-discrepancy in the Embodied Cognition Group than in the Cognitive Only (Cohen’s d = 2.09), and the Control Group (Cohen’s d = 1.46). The Relational sub-category of self-accountability showed no change across groups and suggests virtually no difference in self-discrepancy (Embodied Cognition Group vs. Cognitive Only Cohen’s d = 0.02, Embodied Cognition vs. Control Group Cohen’s d = 0.05). The Secure Identity sub-category showed a larger decrease in self-discrepancy in the Embodied Cognition Group vs. the Cognitive Only Group (Cohen’s d = 1.73), and the Control Group (Cohen’s d = 1.46). Finally, participants reported that the intervention in the Embodied Cognition Group was feasible and acceptable. The implications of these findings support a full randomized controlled trial study so that findings may be generalized across populations to improve the well-being of women and girls.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la autocompasión frenar el síndrome del impostor?
stories.headline: La autocompasión reduce la relación entre el fenómeno del impostor y la ansiedad social
stories.finding: En una muestra de 1408 estudiantes universitarios, el fenómeno del impostor se asoció negativamente con la autocompasión y positivamente con la vergüenza y la ansiedad social. Los análisis de regresión jerárquica mostraron que la autocompasión predijo disminuciones en la ansiedad social.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fomentar la autocompasión en intervenciones universitarias podría mitigar el impacto del síndrome del impostor y reducir la ansiedad social, mejorando la salud mental de los estudiantes.
stories.paperTitle: Associations among impostor phenomenon, self-compassion, shame, and social anxiety in college students
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Social anxiety represents a common internalizing emotional issue among college students, while the imposter phenomenon, as a negative self-cognitive pattern, is regarded as a key psychological factor associated with the triggering and sustaining of social anxiety. Although previous research has preliminarily explored the relationship between the two, the associations among these variables through which self-conscious emotions operate within this association remain insufficiently explained. Grounded in the Cognitive-Affective System Theory of Personality, this study systematically examines the relationships between imposter phenomenon, self-compassion, shame, and social anxiety. Methods: Using a stratified random sampling approach, the study conducted an online questionnaire survey across multiple universities, obtaining 1408 valid responses. The study conducted regression analyses using SPSS. Results: Hierarchical regression analysis revealed that when self-compassion and shame were entered into the regression models, impostor phenomenon was negatively associated with self-compassion and positively associated with shame and social anxiety. Self-compassion was negatively associated with both shame and social anxiety, while shame was positively associated with social anxiety. Moreover, gender significantly moderates the relationship between impostor phenomenon and both self-compassion and social anxiety. Discussion: By shedding new light on the complex relationship between the imposter phenomenon and social anxiety, these findings may inform student mental health support in college students.

stories.hook: ¿La alexitimia predice el burnout en enfermeras oncológicas?
stories.headline: Alexitimia se asocia moderadamente con mayor burnout en enfermeras de oncología
stories.finding: En una muestra de 80 enfermeras oncológicas se encontró una correlación positiva moderada entre los niveles de alexitimia y el burnout ocupacional (r = 0.418). Además, el burnout se relacionó significativamente con la fatiga por compasión y con variables demográficas como edad y estado civil.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que evaluar la alexitimia podría identificar a enfermeras vulnerables al burnout, facilitando intervenciones preventivas y mejorando la salud mental del personal oncológico.
stories.paperTitle: Alexithymia Levels in Oncology Nurses and Their Impact on Occupational Burnout, Compassion Satisfaction and Compassion Fatigue: A Cross-Sectional Study
stories.journal: Turkiye Klinikleri Journal of Nursing Sciences
stories.originalAbstract: Objective: Nurses working with cancer patients face unique psychological and emotional challenges due to the intense nature of their work environment. Alexithymia, characterized by difficulty in identifying and expressing emotions, may significantly impact these nurses' professional well-being. This study aims to explore the correlation between the levels of alexithymia and the experiences of occupational burnout, compassion satisfaction, and compassion fatigue among nurses in oncology settings. Material and Methods: A descriptive and correlational research design was employed at Gaziantep University Şahinbey Research and Application Hospital. The study involved 80 nurses from different oncology services. Assessment tools included the Toronto Alexithymia Scale, Maslach Burnout Inventory, Compassion Satisfaction Scale, and Compassion Fatigue-Short Scale. Results: The study found a moderate positive correlation between alexithymia and occupational burnout (r=0.418). Additionally, significant relationships were noted between burnout and compassion fatigue, and various demographic factors (age, marital status, voluntary work in oncology) were found to influence alexithymia and burnout levels. Conclusion: The findings highlight the need for targeted psychological support and interventions for nurses in oncology settings, given the identified relationship between alexithymia, burnout, and compassion fatigue. This study contributes to the understanding of the emotional dynamics in high-stress healthcare environments and emphasizes the importance of addressing these issues to improve patient care quality.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la participación paterna disminuir el miedo al compromiso?
stories.headline: La competencia emocional media la relación entre implicación paterna y temor al compromiso
stories.finding: En una muestra de 397 jóvenes adultos (20‑24 años), la implicación paterna se asoció negativamente con el temor al compromiso (r = ‑0.638, p < 0.001). El análisis de mediación mostró que la competencia emocional explica parcialmente esta relación, reduciendo el miedo cuando la implicación del padre es mayor.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que fortalecer la competencia emocional y fomentar la participación paterna en la adolescencia puede prevenir la ansiedad de compromiso en la adultez, ofreciendo un objetivo terapéutico para intervenciones de prevención y terapia de pareja.
stories.paperTitle: The Role of Emotional Competence as a Mediator between Father Involvement and Fear of Relationship Commitment
stories.originalAbstract: Early adulthood is a crucial phase marked by the demands of building intimate and committed relationships. However, an increasing number of individuals at this stage experience fear of relationship commitment, a fear of long-term relationships characterized by anxiety about emotional closeness, loss of autonomy, and relationship uncertainty. This condition impacts the quality of interpersonal relationships and decreases psychological well-being, emotional stability, and family well-being. This study aims to examine the mediating role of emotional competence in the relationship between father involvement and fear of relationship commitment in emerging adulthood. This correlational study design with 397 participants aged 20–24 years (M = 22.04; SD = 1.070), recruited through accidental sampling. Data were collected using the Inventory of Father Involvement (IFI), Short Profile of Emotional Competence (SPEC), and Fear of Relationship Commitment Scale (LFRC). Data analysis was conducted using mediation analysis PROCESS Hayes model 4 software, SPSS version 25. The results showed that father involvement was negatively associated with fear of relationship commitment (r = -0.638, p < 0.001). Mediation analysis indicated that emotional competence partially mediated the relationship between father involvement and fear of relationship commitment (β = -0.155; 95% CI [-0.228, -0.096]). These findings highlight the importance of father involvement in enhancing emotional competence and reducing fear of commitment.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo elige la gente cooperar o competir en tiempo real?
stories.headline: Modelo computacional predice decisiones cooperativas y competitivas con 87 % de precisión
stories.finding: En un juego continuo de forrajeo, 58 díadas (116 participantes) se organizaron en tres estrategias: cooperativa, intermedia y competitiva. Un modelo computacional que incluye minimización de trayectorias, comunicación sensorimotora e historial de elecciones predijo las decisiones con 87 % de exactitud, vinculando la certeza con la coordinación espaciotemporal.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo muestra que la cooperación y competencia pueden modelarse con precisión mediante variables sensorimotoras, ofreciendo una herramienta robusta para estudiar dinámicas sociales reales y diseñar intervenciones que fomenten la colaboración eficaz.
stories.paperTitle: Continuous dynamics of cooperation and competition in social decision-making
stories.originalAbstract: Real-life social interactions often unfold continuously and involve dynamic cooperation and competition, yet most studies rely on discrete games that do not capture the adaptive and graded nature of continuous sensorimotor decisions. To address this gap, we developed the Cooperation-Competition Foraging game-an ecologically grounded paradigm in which pairs of participants (dyads) navigate a continuous shared space under face-to-face visibility, deciding in real-time to collect rewarded targets either individually or jointly. Dyads (n = 58, 116 participants) spontaneously converged on distinct stable strategies along the cooperation-competition spectrum, forming three groups: cooperative, intermediate, and competitive. Despite the behavioral complexity, our computational model, which incorporated travel path minimization, sensorimotor communication, and recent choice history, predicted dyadic decisions with 87% accuracy, and linked prediction certainty with ensuing dynamics of spatiotemporal coordination. Further modeling revealed how sensorimotor factors, such as movement speed and skill, shape distinct strategies and payoffs. Crucially, we quantify the cost of cooperation, demonstrating that in many dyads prosocial tendencies outweigh the individual benefits of exploiting skill advantages. Our versatile framework provides a predictive, mechanistic account of how social and embodied drivers promote the emergence of dynamic cooperation and competition, and offers rigorous metrics for investigating the neural basis of naturalistic social interactions, and for linking personality traits to distinct strategies.

stories.headline: Desconexión en Minecraft impulsada por factores sociales y de juego
stories.finding: Entrevistas semiestructuradas con 15 participantes mostraron que la ausencia de amigos, la sobreexposición y los contratiempos motivan el desapego, mientras que la novedad, la progresión y el combate estimulan la permanencia. El estudio propone considerar la desconexión como parte natural del recorrido del usuario.
stories.takeaway: Reconocer la desconexión como fenómeno natural ayuda a diseñar experiencias más sostenibles y a apoyar a los jugadores en su gestión del tiempo y bienestar.
stories.paperTitle: Pixels and people: Exploring the dynamics of engagement and disengagement in Minecraft's multiplayer realm
stories.originalAbstract: • Disengagement is a multicausal player choice, not a design failure • Disengagement can be supported by various game design features • Internal, external, motivational, emotional factors influence dis(engagement) • (Dis)engagement triggers, supports and suppressors are identified Engagement is often viewed as the holy grail of digital experiences, particularly video games, while disengagement is seen as a consequence of poor design. This study attempts to flip the script, exploring disengagement as a natural part of the user journey rather than a failure of game design. Focusing on the popular open-world game Minecraft, the research investigates dynamics triggering engagement and disengagement in the multiplayer mode through the lenses of established frameworks like the Process Model of Engagement as well as the Mechanics, Dynamics, and Aesthetics model. Semi-structured focus-group interviews conducted with 15 participants analyzed using Mayring's content analysis revealed social connections, novelty, progression, goal-driven gameplay, and adrenaline-fueled combat as key drivers that keep players hooked. Yet, the very act of achieving goals, absence of friends, overplay, setbacks, skill gaps, negative interactions, and the demands of the real world can trigger a powerful urge to disengage. Far from a design flaw, this research expands the body of literature suggesting that disengagement is a vital component of user autonomy. By redefining success beyond mere engagement metrics, the study paves the way for responsible gaming practices that empower players to make informed choices about their level of involvement. It beckons us to embrace a holistic vision of genuinely sustainable, ethical, and meaningful digital experiences that respect user autonomy and cultivate healthy engagement patterns.

stories.hook: ¿Puede la reflexión mental reducir el duelo prolongado?
stories.headline: La función reflexiva media la relación entre apego inseguro y duelo prolongado
stories.finding: En una muestra de 329 adultos en duelo, la certeza sobre estados mentales medió completamente la asociación entre el apego evitativo y ansioso y la gravedad de los síntomas de duelo prolongado. Los resultados sugieren que la disfunción en la función reflexiva es un mecanismo clave.
stories.takeaway: Identificar y entrenar la certeza reflexiva podría mejorar intervenciones terapéuticas para personas con apego inseguro, reduciendo la intensidad del duelo prolongado y favoreciendo la resiliencia.
stories.paperTitle: Reflective functioning mediates the relationship between insecure adult attachment and the severity of prolonged grief symptoms
stories.originalAbstract: Background: This study aimed to investigate the mediation role of reflective functioning (i.e., certainty and uncertainty about mental states) in the relationship between insecure attachment (i.e., attachment avoidance and attachment anxiety ) and the severity of prolonged grief symptoms. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted with 329 bereaved participants (51.7% females, mean age= 46.94 ± 14.62 years). Participants completed the Prolonged Grief Scale (PG-13), the Attachment Style Questionnaire (ASQ), and the Reflective Functioning Questionnaire (RFQ). Demographic and bereavement-related information were also collected. Results: Certainty about mental states fully mediated the relationship between both the attachment avoidance and attachement anxiety and severity of prolonged grief symptoms. Conclusions: The findings of this study indicate that reflective functioning impairment, specifically certainty about mental states of self and others, mediate the paths from insecure attachment to prolonged grief symptoms. This suggests that improving reflective functioning may contribute to the treatment bereaved individuals at risk of PGD.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo aligerar la carga cognitiva de estudiantes con TDAH en línea?
stories.headline: Nuevo marco inclusivo reduce la carga cognitiva en estudiantes neurodivergentes
stories.finding: Los autores crean un marco inclusivo que gestiona la carga cognitiva de estudiantes neurodivergentes, incluido el TDAH, en educación en línea. El modelo define seis áreas críticas y, mediante un análisis PESTEL, muestra retos como la escasez de recursos, la falta de compromiso institucional y la normativa de accesibilidad.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo orienta a docentes y diseñadores de cursos a estructurar contenidos y entornos que minimicen la sobrecarga cognitiva, favoreciendo la atención y el aprendizaje de estudiantes con TDAH y otras neurodivergencias.
stories.paperTitle: Cognitive load and neurodiversity in online education: a preliminary framework for educational research and policy
stories.originalAbstract: This theoretical paper presents the development and analysis of an inclusive educational framework designed to manage cognitive load for neurodivergent students in online learning environments. Drawing from cognitive load theory and neurodiversity studies, the framework is based on existing literature, empirical work conducted by the authors, and iterative feedback from a participatory research advisory board. Taking a neurodiversity-informed perspective that focuses on interventions addressing challenges common across a range of conditions, it identifies six critical areas that might impact cognitive load in online learning for neurodivergent students: format, environment, delivery, instruction, support, and research (FEDIS+R). To assess the external factors influencing the potential implementation of the framework and its place within the broader landscape of inclusive education, a PESTEL (Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, and Legal) analysis was conducted. The analysis highlights challenges such as resource disparities, institutional commitment to inclusion, and legal requirements for accessibility, which may affect the adoption of the framework. Given the evolving nature of both cognitive load theory and neurodiversity studies, future research directions are suggested to evaluate its effectiveness across diverse educational contexts. This paper contributes to the growing body of knowledge on neurodiversity in education and offers practical recommendations for educators and policymakers seeking to create inclusive online learning environments.

stories.hook: ¿El estilo autoritario potencia la inteligencia emocional?
stories.headline: El estilo autoritario se asocia a mayores niveles de inteligencia emocional en adolescentes
stories.finding: En una muestra de 121 adolescentes (12‑20 años) se aplicaron el Parenting Authority Questionnaire y el Schutte Self‑Report Emotional Intelligence Test. Los resultados mostraron correlaciones significativas entre el estilo autoritario y varios dominios de la inteligencia emocional.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo sugiere que combinar calidez emocional con límites claros favorece el desarrollo de competencias emocionales, orientando a profesionales y padres a promover estilos autoritarios equilibrados para mejorar la adaptación psicológica de los adolescentes.
stories.paperTitle: Emotional Intelligence Among Adolescents Reared By Authoritative Parenting Style
stories.journal: Educational Administration Theory and Practice journal
stories.originalAbstract: Background: Parenting is a way of preparing the child independent in varied ways such as physical, social, psychological as well as emotional. As parents, it becomes the responsibility of the parents to provide them with a healthy environment to grow and become self-sufficient. Objective: This study is intended to evaluate the correlation between various domains of emotional intelligence among children reared by authoritative parenting style. Method: In the present piece of study a sample of 121 aged between (12-20) years (M = 16; SD = 2.73) was included. The sample was collected through the Non-probability (Purposive) sampling technique. The Parenting Authority Questionnaire (PAQ) developed by (Buri, 1991) and the Schutte Self-Report Emotional Intelligence Test (SSEIT) constructed by (Schutte et al., 1998) were administered to collect the information from the participants. Results: The outcomes of the study reported a correlation between various domains of emotional intelligence at varied significant values. Conclusion: It may be concluded that combining emotional warmth with appropriate limits and boundaries helps the child to express themselves healthily, the way seen in children raised by authoritative parents.

stories.hook: ¿Cómo la inflamación afecta la recuperación cerebral?
stories.headline: La inflamación obstaculiza la neuroplasticidad tras lesión cerebral traumática
stories.finding: La revisión muestra que la neuroinflamación, indicada por biomarcadores como SAA1 y TLR4, deteriora la neuroplasticidad y la recuperación tras lesión cerebral traumática en humanos y animales. Bloquear vías inflamatorias, como NLRP3 y la microglía, podría habilitar tratamientos personalizados y optimizar la neurorehabilitación.
stories.takeaway: Este hallazgo subraya que la modulación de la inflamación es clave para potenciar la plasticidad cerebral y personalizar la rehabilitación tras TBI, ofreciendo una vía terapéutica para mejorar la recuperación funcional.
stories.paperTitle: The Role of Neuroinflammation in Shaping Neuroplasticity and Recovery Outcomes Following Traumatic Brain Injury: A Systematic Review
stories.originalAbstract: Neuroplasticity and neuroinflammation are variables seen during recovery from traumatic brain injury (TBI), while biomarkers are useful in monitoring injury and guiding rehabilitation efforts. This systematic review examines how neuroinflammation affects neuroplasticity and recovery following TBI in animal models and humans. Studies were identified from an online search of the PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase databases without any search time range. This review has been registered on Open OSF (n) UDWQM. Recent studies highlight the critical role of biomarkers like serum amyloid A1 (SAA1) and Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) in predicting TBI patients' injury severity and recovery outcomes, offering the potential for personalized treatment and improved neurorehabilitation strategies. Additionally, insights from animal studies reveal how neuroinflammation affects recovery, emphasizing targets such as NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 (NLRP3) and microglia for enhancing therapeutic interventions. This review emphasizes the central role of neuroinflammation in TBI, and its adverse impact on neuroplasticity and recovery, and suggests that targeted anti-inflammatory treatments and biomarker-based personalized approaches hold the key to improvement. Such approaches will need further development in future research by integrating neuromodulation and pharmacological interventions, along with biomarker validation, to optimize management in TBI.
